RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the July 5, 2004/Asadha 14, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Culture; Development of North-Eastern
Region; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Human Resource Development;
Information and Broadcasting; Law and Justice; Parliamentary Affairs;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Urban Development;
Urban Employment and Poverty Alleviation.)
Total number of questions—20
1
Changes in text books
*1. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA:
Will  the  Minister  of  HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the large scale changes made by the NCERT
in the various text books prescribed for the
school students;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government’s reaction thereto; and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
to correct these changes, if warranted, so
as to ensure the factual accuracy and
objectivity of such books?
India on priority watch list over IPRs
*2. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether United States has once again
put India on the priority watch list of its
301 provision of the trade laws over
inadequate protection of intellectual
property rights;
(b) whether amendments in the Indian
Patent laws which became effective from
May, 2003 have been considered inadequate
by the U.S.; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps Government propose to take to
further improve its patent laws?
Licenses to prostitutes
†*3. PROF. RAM DEO BHANDARY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
legalise prostitution by providing licenses
to the women engaged in this profession;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have made any
alternative arrangements to get them proper
status in the society;
(d) whether they are now being provided
with licenses after the failure of the above
arrangements; and

Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
†*4. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the funds provided under ‘Sarva
Shiksha Abhiyan’ to various States,
particularly to Himachal Pradesh during the
last two years; and
(b) the details of Government’s plan to
achieve the target of this scheme and the
progress made so far in various States,
particularly in Himachal Pradesh?
Conditional Access System
*5. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Telecom Regulatory
Authority  of  India in its consultation
paper on broadcasting raised issues like
making CAS voluntary and subjecting pay
channels and advertisements to price
regulation besides a host of quality-related
matters;
(b) if so, to what extent the Telecom
Regulatory Authority has sought views in
regard to CAS being made voluntary;
(c) whether any concrete steps and
measures have been taken for making CAS
voluntary; and
(d) by when, a final decision is likely to
be taken in this regard?
Basic amenities in resettlement
colonies
*6. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Will
the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that DDA is not providing basic
amenities like electricity, water and roads
to the resettlement colonies in Delhi even
after four years; and
(b) if so, by when the same would be
provided?
Theft in the Viswa  Bharati Museum
*7. SHRIMATI  N. P.  DURGA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a theft took
place in Viswa Bharati and many valuable
and priceless items such as Tagore's Nobel
medallion and others memorabilia have been
stolen from the museum; and
(b) if so, the action Government have
taken in co-ordination with the State
Government to catch the culprits?
Production in Public Sector industries
†*8. SHRI RA VI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of HEAVY
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is  a fact that the Public
Sector industries have registered
considerable growth in production during
the recent years;

Chinese investment in infrastructure
sector
1. SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether China has called for
expanding bilateral ties with India in the
infrastructure sector, keeping in view a
spurt in East Asian countries' construction
industry after its accession to the World
Trade Organisation;
(b) if so, whether China International
Construction Association (CHINCA) Vice
Chairman has pointed out that Chinese
companies were keen to explore projects
with Indian companies on BOT basis in
the areas including railways, housing,
hospitals and bridges;
(c) if so, whether Government have
accepted the Chinese proposal;
(d) if so, whether any agreement has
been reached; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Financial assistance to coffee growers
2. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have extended
a special financial assistance to the coffee
growers to tide over the economic crisis in
the sector during 2003-04;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the extent of subsidy given to the
coffee growers during 2003-04;
(d) whether any interest free loans were
given by the Coffee Board in 2003-04; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Marine exports
3. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the marine products exports during
2003-04 and foreign exchange earnings;
(b) whether it is a fact that many
countries have banned Indian marine

2

products on the grounds of not maintaining
high standards of hygiene;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
mitigate such problems?
Shifting MPEDA to Vishakhapatnam
4. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to shift
the MPEDA from Cochin to
Vishakhapatnam;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that most of the
marine product exports originate from the
East Coast; and
(d) if so, the steps taken to shift
MPEDA to the East Coast?
New Trade Policy
5. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
revamped the trade policy;
(b) if so, whether a twenty five Member
Advisory Group had been constituted to
advise on the export and import related
issues;
(c) whether the new policy would focus
on agriculture and employment generation;
(d) whether Government are also
considering for promotion of FDI that
promotes agriculture exports and creates
additonal jobs; and
(e) if so, by when the New Trade Policy
is likely to be announced?
Coffee and tea production
6.  PROF.M.M. AGARWAL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of coffee/tea
production and consumption during the
last three years;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any policy to increase the coffee/
tea production;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of the measures being
taken by Government to give some relief
to the coffee/tea growers?
Wheat export
7. PROF. M. M. AGARWAL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the surplus wheat
available for exports during the year
2004-05;
(b) the details of the surplus wheat
exported to various countries during the
last three years; and
(c) the value of the foreign exchange
earned in Indian currency during this
period?
Expansion of G-20
8. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps Government are planning
to expand G-20 and building linkages with
other developing countries of the world;
and
(b) the steps Government are planning
to adopt India specific approach in the
